messages:
maria (PM): Quick sync — we need a trimmed GA checklist that calls out SLA, docs, support, monitoring, and pricing gaps. Who can own each lane?

sam (Eng Lead): I can take SLA/latency targets. Quick question: do we lock to p95 150ms for hosted or allow tiered SLOs?

kevin (SRE): Tiered makes sense. For Dedicated/Private customers we should default to an availability SLO + request latency tiers. Also need runbook for failover to fallback model.

lee (Docs): I can land the GA docs but need the final SLA language and example config snippets from eng. If we pick tiers, I need wording for both hosted/dedicated/private.

sophie (Pricing): Pricing needs the unit economics for each SLA tier (cost delta for low-latency rigs). If we do a guaranteed p95, that should be priced as a premium.

nate (Support): Support will own oncall routing + playbook. We need to know escalation matrix and who covers cross-region incidents pre-GA. Also training doc for Level 1.

maria (PM): Proposal: hosted = Standard (p95 250ms), Priority (p95 120ms). Dedicated = SLA-backed availability + latency target (custom). Private = passthrough to ops/contract. Owners: sam (SLA), lee (docs), kevin (monitoring/runbooks), sophie (pricing), nate (support).

sam (Eng Lead): Ok. For hosted Priority we'll enable extra GPU hot-pools + preemptive prefix caching. That increases infra cost ~20-35% depending on workload. I'll produce a cost/latency tradeoff table by EOD.

kevin (SRE): Monitoring: need synthetic p95/p99 checks across regions + KV cache hit-rate dashboards. I'll add alerts: 5m p95 regression -> severity 2, sustained 15m -> sev1. Runbook draft pushed to the runbooks repo.

lee (Docs): Action: I will draft SLA appendix and sample API error responses. Need sample JSON for SLA breach payloads. Can someone paste an example?

sam (Eng Lead): sample SLA breach payload:```{
  "customer_id": "cust_123",
  "period": "2026-04-01/2026-04-30",
  "p95_latency_ms": 180,
  "slo_target_ms": 120,
  "credit": "0.05% of monthly invoice"
}```Use that as a placeholder.

sophie (Pricing): We'll map tiers: Standard (baseline, token-based), Priority (+40% unit price), Dedicated (contracted, tiered discount). I'll populate a spreadsheet with sample invoices for common rps patterns.

nate (Support): For GA support model: 9-5 L1 triage (chat), 24/7 incident paging for sev1 if customer on Priority or Dedicated. Need to document handoff to SRE on-call.

maria (PM): Two outstanding tradeoffs: 1) pricing uplift vs adoption friction for Priority. 2) strict p95 for hosted can force lots of cold-start work. We should consider gradual opt-in for Priority during first 30d GA. Thoughts?

sam (Eng Lead): Gradual opt-in seems reasonable. Start with an invite-only Priority pilot (2–3 customers) to validate infra patterns. We can extend after 30d.

kevin (SRE): Agreed. Pilot lets us tune alert thresholds and fallback behavior without mass exposure. Also good to test regional failover.

sophie (Pricing): Pilot also helps us test billing pipes and refund/credit automation for SLA breaches. I want at least one enterprise customer in the pilot.

lee (Docs): I'll draft a pilot-specific doc section: "How Priority pilot works" + known limitations and expectations.

nate (Support): For pilot, we'll have dedicated oncall rotation for the customers. I'll align training sessions with SRE next week.

deploy-bot: smoke-tests scheduled: hosted-priority-smoke @ 2026-05-06T02:00Z; notify channel #deploys on failures.

maria (PM): Next steps and owners: sam -> SLA detail + tradeoff table (EOD); kevin -> monitoring + runbook (tomorrow); lee -> draft SLA + pilot docs (tomorrow); sophie -> pricing spreadsheet + pilot invoice samples (tomorrow); nate -> pilot oncall plan + L1 playbook (tomorrow). I'll consolidate into GA checklist and schedule review Friday.

sam (Eng Lead): noted. I'll also include a short list of mitigations for cold-starts (prefix caching, warm pools, shorter idle GC).

kevin (SRE): Ping me when the draft runbook is ready, I'll iterate.

lee (Docs): tagging @maria for copy review once I have SLA wording.

sophie (Pricing): I'll share a short customer-facing pricing blurb for the docs.

nate (Support): Will prepare a canned escalation email and standardized incident template.

maria (PM): Great. If nothing else, we'll meet Fri 10:00 for final sign-off. Please update your assigned doc/checklist items beforehand. :thumbsup:

sam (Eng Lead): 👍

kevin (SRE): 👍

lee (Docs): 👍

sophie (Pricing): 👍

nate (Support): 👍

maria (PM): Thanks team — will post the consolidated checklist as a thread reply when ready.
